03d1e364e2.q: What percentage of advisors departing wire houses stayed in W-2 employment in 2024?
03d1e364e2.a: 57% of advisors that left a wire house or W-2 shop stayed in another W-2 channel, compared to 60% the previous year. About one-third, 36%, went independent. This shows that the majority of departing advisors remained within the W-2 model rather than transitioning to independence.

e4edc4fb4d.q: Why are wire house firms recruiting fewer experienced advisors despite offering aggressive compensation deals?
e4edc4fb4d.a: Wire house firms are recruiting 15% fewer experienced advisors year-over-year even with deals starting at four handles (400%+), because advisors are voting with their feet toward regional and alternative W-2 platforms. Firms like Raymond James and RBC offer more stable compensation plans that rarely change, whereas wire houses move compensation goalposts annually, requiring advisors to produce 10-15% more to maintain payout levels.
